title: France's Foncier innovant aerial-image AI detects 140,000 undeclared pools and about €40 million in extra property tax by 20 March 2024; Dordogne alone 1,500 in 2023
summary: Minister Cazenave (20 March 2024): DGFiP's AI tool detected 140,000 undeclared pools, c. €40m extra property tax for local authorities; Dordogne found 1,500 in 2023. No commune-level figure found.
account: On 20 March 2024 Thomas Cazenave, minister for public accounts, presented the first bilan of the government's anti-fraud plan at Bercy. He said the DGFiP's algorithmic tool, Foncier innovant, introduced in October 2021, had detected 140,000 undeclared swimming pools. The tool detects pools and buildings on IGN aerial photographs and compares them with declarations. An agent then checks each detection. That would let local authorities collect about €40 million in property tax. Owners received DGFiP letters asking them to regularize (RMC, Ouest-France, L'Indépendant, 21 March 2024). CNews (11 June 2024) cites the DGFiP annual activity report as reported by Ouest-France. It gives 140,000 pools identified in 2023 and €40 million that should have been paid in 2023. That compares with 20,000 pools in the 2022 experiment in nine départements (20 Minutes). L'Indépendant instead states 120,000 for 2022, so the press accounts of the yearly split disagree. At département level, ici (France Bleu) reported on 24 March 2024 on the Dordogne public-finance office. It had found about 1,500 undeclared pools in 2023 among some 30,000 in the département. It would send property-tax catch-up notices by the end of March. No official DGFiP or ministry document is among the sources, as the ministry's website was not available. No commune-level result was found.
purpose: Detect undeclared pools and buildings from aerial imagery so that they are added to the cadastral base and taxed. This was the tool's intended purpose.
system: Foncier innovant (DGFiP deep-learning detection of pools and buildings on IGN aerial photographs, built with Capgemini and Google)
developer: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) with Capgemini and Google
deployer: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), ministère de l'Économie et des Finances
domain: Public finance: property-tax base and anti-fraud
taxonomy_note: Tax yield is read as the authority's revenue; Trustible's description is written for product sales.

ratings.reason: Owners of detected pools bear a cost; no individual beneficiary is documented.
Material to the DGFiP and to local authorities. The minister attributed about €40 million of additional property tax to the tool. Dordogne alone is recovering tax on about 1,500 pools.
About €40 million nationally is small against total property-tax receipts. The press accounts disagree on the yearly split.

ai_role.statement: The AI detects pool outlines on aerial photographs and compares them with declarations. An agent verifies each detection before the construction is added to the cadastral value (Ouest-France). The 140,000 pools and €40 million are the minister's own attribution to the tool, relayed by several news outlets. CNews cites the DGFiP annual report via Ouest-France. No official document is among the sources. A CGT Finances publiques official told Ouest-France that field colleagues put the algorithm's error threshold at 55–60%. So the detections required substantial human checking. No commune-level outcome is on record. The Dordogne figure is the most local one read.

produced_by: IGN aerial photographs covering the whole territory
A detection model built with Capgemini and Google, generalized nationally after the 2022 nine-département experiment
Comparison of detected outlines with cadastral declarations
Agent verification of each detection and letters inviting owners to regularize
must_hold: A false-detection rate low enough for agents to verify (a union official cites 55–60% errors)
Legal basis to add undeclared constructions to the cadastral value
Local offices with capacity to send and handle catch-up notices

echoes.setting: 2022 experiment in nine départements: about 20,000 undeclared pools, about €10 million
Dordogne département, 2023 campaign: about 1,500 undeclared pools, catch-up notices sent by end of March 2024
Announced extension of the same tool from pools to undeclared buildings (garages, verandas); no outcome yet

headline: Foncier innovant finds 140,000 undeclared pools
metric: detected 140,000 undeclared pools, c. €40m extra property tax

comparator.against: a surveyor noticing a new pool in a neighborhood by eye and checking the cadastre
comparator.before: le géomètre qui remarquait une nouvelle piscine dans un quartier et devait vérifier dans le cadastre si elle était déclarée ou pas
comparator.after: Dans toute la France, 140.000 piscines clandestines ont été repérées, ce qui va rapporter 40 millions d'euros.
comparator.quote: Fini, le géomètre qui remarquait une nouvelle piscine dans un quartier et devait vérifier dans le cadastre si elle était déclarée ou pas. Désormais, les impôts utilisent des photos prises par avion et analysées par l'intelligence artificielle qui repère automatiquement les carrés bleus des piscines et les compare aux fichiers existants.

later.note: In June 2024 the DGFiP's 2023 activity report, as relayed by 20 Minutes and CNews, restated the 140,000 pools and the 40 million euros of property tax, against 20,000 pools in 2022, and the plan to extend detection to undeclared buildings.
later.quote: 140.000 piscines non déclarées ont été épinglées par le fisc en 2023, a dévoilé la Direction générale des finances publiques ce mardi dans son rapport d’activité 2023 relayé par Ouest-France.

fields.account: On 20 March 2024 Thomas Cazenave, minister for public accounts, presented the first bilan of the government's anti-fraud plan at Bercy. He said the DGFiP's algorithmic tool, Foncier innovant, introduced in October 2021, had detected 140,000 undeclared swimming pools. The tool detects pools and buildings on IGN aerial photographs and compares them with declarations. An agent then checks each detection. That would let local authorities collect about €40 million in property tax. Owners received DGFiP letters asking them to regularize (RMC, Ouest-France, L'Indépendant, 21 March 2024). CNews (11 June 2024) cites the DGFiP annual activity report as reported by Ouest-France. It gives 140,000 pools identified in 2023 and €40 million that should have been paid in 2023. That compares with 20,000 pools in the 2022 experiment in nine départements (20 Minutes). L'Indépendant instead states 120,000 for 2022, so the press accounts of the yearly split disagree. At département level, ici (France Bleu) reported on 24 March 2024 on the Dordogne public-finance office. It had found about 1,500 undeclared pools in 2023 among some 30,000 in the département. It would send property-tax catch-up notices by the end of March. No official DGFiP or ministry document is among the sources, as the ministry's website was not available. No commune-level result was found.
